patch_description: Building on the observation that all prior single-shared-parameter ("theta") designs plateau at a 0.80 combined score with perfect train/val/test accuracy, this version tests the recommended two-shared-parameter split: one scalar "theta_r" drives all single-qubit rotations (RX, RY, RZ axes reused across every qubit) while a second, independent scalar "theta_e" drives a single non-local parametrized entangling sweep (CRZ at distance-2). This gives the optimizer a genuinely separate rotation-vs-entanglement degree of freedom (only 2 unique parameter names per block instead of 1) while simultaneously *shrinking* the circuit: the heavy multi-layer fixed entangling stack (nearest-neighbor CZ ring + skip-2 CZ ring + antipodal CZ shortcuts + parametrized CRZ sweep) used in earlier variants is collapsed into a single nearest-neighbor CZ ring (for baseline connectivity, zero-param) plus one parametrized CRZ skip-2 sweep (for tunable long-range entanglement). This roughly halves gate count and depth relative to the current program (from ~264 gates / depth 114 down to ~40 gates / depth ~40), which should speed up convergence and reduce any residual optimization difficulty, while keeping parameter count as low as physically sensible (2 unique names per block) and preserving the full 3-axis single-qubit rotation basis and ring+long-range entangling topology that empirically achieved perfect accuracy in prior seeds.
